items.description: 1. Who is the regulator for insurance industry in India? - IRDAI (IRDA TO IRDAI IN 2014)
2. Which is the secondary burden of risk? - Setting aside reserves to meet potential losses of future.
3. Risk transfer through risk pooling is Insurance.
4. Insurance pays when? - When there is loss of life or asset.
5. One of the characteristics of traditional insurance - Low yields because inflation and interest rates affect real savings in insurance maturity benefits.
6. Advantages of insurance - security, savings, and tax benefits.
7. Who devised HLV concept? - Prof. Huebner
8. Why young people are charged less premium? - Premium is related to mortality. Smaller the age, lower the mortality risk.
9. In a valid contract, the element that deals with premium is - Consideration.
10. Pressure applied through criminal means to force a contract? - Coercion.
11. Uncertainty and level or extent of damage are two components of Risk.
12. Who cannot sign a contract? - Minor, mentally unstable person, and people disqualified by law.
13. Who is not having insurable interest? - Cousin, uncle, brother, sister, close friend, neighbor etc. (Unless financial dependency is proved).
14. An individual with an aggressive risk profile chooses - Wealth accumulation products (like ULIPs).
15. Insurance is the only contingency product.
16. Inflation means raise in prices due to change in economy over a period of time.
17. Higher the risk covered, higher the premium paid.
18. Term insurance can be bought both as a main policy and a rider.
19. A term policy can be converted into a whole life policy (if option is provided in terms).
20. An individual who needs maximum insurance with a low budget can opt for - Term plan.
21. Moneyback plan is a kind of endowment plan which gives money at frequent intervals. Installments given earlier are not deducted if death occurs in between.
22. A person normally saves for immediate needs, contingencies, and future goals.
23. In a traditional plan, the rate of return is not easy to ascertain. So also bonus calculation and surrender value. In short, it is not transparent.
24. Universal life policy was introduced in USA, in the year 1977.
25. All universal life policies are termed in India as variable insurance plans.
26. ULIP is a kind of variable life insurance plan.
27. In ULIP, investment risk is borne by the investor/policyholder, not by the insurer.
28. Allocation of funds in ULIPs is investor's choice.
29. Changing of funds in ULIP from equity to debt or vice-versa is called - Switching.
30. Only educated, risk-taking, and market-knowing people prefer ULIPs.
31. In ULIP, in case of death, the insurance amount payable is Sum Assured or Fund Value, whichever is higher.
32. Risk of early death cannot be covered by taking a pure retirement/annuity plan.
33. In an Ordinary Annuity (Annuity Immediate), equal cash flows are paid at the end of each equal time interval.
34. In a health/medical policy, 30 days is allowed as grace time for renewal.
35. Paying policy premium within the allowed extended days after due date is Renewal. Non-payment within this time leads to - Lapse.
36. Paying premium on lapsed policies to make them active again is - Revival.
37. To revive a policy, one has to pay reinstatement charges, past premium dues, and interest thereon.
38. Ordinary, special, installment, and loan-cum-revival are 4 ways available to revive a policy.
39. General Insurance contracts are indemnity contracts. Life insurance contracts are value contracts.
40. If moral hazard aspect is not looked into during underwriting, it may result in - Adverse Selection.
41. Primary care center is the place where one goes for initial/basic treatment.
42. Network hospitals give treatment without upfront payment because they have signed MOUs with insurers.
43. Cashless facility means bills are paid directly by the Insurance Company/TPA to network hospitals.
44. TPA means Third Party Administrator.
45. Portability means changing health policy from one Company to another without losing continuity benefits (like waiting period credit).
46. Domiciliary treatment means medical treatment given at home when the patient cannot be moved to a hospital due to serious condition or lack of beds, for a minimum of 3 days.
47. Health insurance policy generally does not cover pre-existing diseases for a specific waiting period (usually up to 48 months).
48. Group insurance policies are cheaper than individual insurance policies.
49. Keyman insurance policy is taken by a business entity on the life of its crucial/key employees to protect against financial loss.
50. Assignment means transferring the rights, title, and benefits of a life insurance policy to another person or institution.
